title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 51 (Promisor not bound to perform, unless reciprocal promisee ready and willing to perform)

content.overview: Section 51 provides that when a contract consists of reciprocal promises to be simultaneously performed, no promisor need perform his promise unless the promisee is ready and willing to perform his reciprocal promise.
content.glance: Simultaneous reciprocal promises → no duty to perform unless the other is ready and willing.
content.study: Where reciprocal promises are to be performed simultaneously, a promisor need not perform unless the promisee is ready and willing to perform the reciprocal promise. Current-law framing: identify simultaneous reciprocal promises; test readiness and willingness of the other party; apply non-obligation if not ready and willing.

sections.heading: Simultaneous reciprocal promises
sections.body: No promisor need perform unless the promisee is ready and willing to perform his reciprocal promise.

provisions.title: Promisor not bound to perform, unless reciprocal promisee ready and willing to perform

examples.title: Sale against payment
examples.body: A is to deliver goods and B is to pay the price simultaneously. A need not deliver unless B is ready and willing to pay under s. 51.

hypotheticals.question: Must both parties complete performance at the same instant?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 51 requires readiness and willingness to perform the reciprocal promise; actual simultaneous completion is not always required before either may proceed.

misconceptions.trap: One party must always perform first in simultaneous reciprocal contracts.
misconceptions.correction: Section 51: neither need perform unless the other is ready and willing.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 51 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify simultaneous reciprocal promises. II. Test readiness and willingness of the other party. III. Apply non-obligation if not ready and willing. IV. Conclude.

examTips: State readiness and willingness as the condition.
